phase: V48AE BLIND SUBJECT ADJUDICATION — PHASE 1 PRE-REGISTRATION
protocol: Labels below were committed BEFORE running production resolver or V2 shadow evaluator. Per user directive §4: 'independent reviewer judges the actual text WITHOUT seeing the engine's judgment.' The labels represent what a human financial analyst would say the subject of the event is, based on text alone.
sample_design: 75 NEW independent cases (25 positive + 25 negative + 25 ambiguous). These cases were NOT used during V48AD rule development. They are designed to represent realistic financial text from central bank press releases (ECB, BoE, BEA, FCA, SEC) and include a natural mix of structures — NOT specifically targeted at V2's added verbs or head nouns.

label_definitions.TRUE_SUBJECT: The candidate IS the semantic subject of the event — the event verb applies to the candidate, and the measurement (if any) describes the candidate.
label_definitions.FALSE_BINDING: The candidate appears in the text but is NOT the subject — the event is about a completely different topic. The candidate is mentioned as background.
label_definitions.AMBIGUOUS: The case has conflicting signals or is genuinely unclear to a human reader — the candidate is mentioned but its role as subject cannot be determined with confidence.
label_definitions.CONTEXT: The candidate appears as a noun modifier or context-only reference (e.g., 'FX turnover data is collected' — FX is a modifier of 'data', not the subject of an action).

cases.text: Real GDP increased 3.2 percent in the second quarter, primarily reflecting positive contributions from consumer spending.
cases.reasoning: The event verb 'increased' applies directly to GDP with a clear measurement '3.2 percent'. GDP is unambiguously the subject.

cases.text: Annual CPI inflation rose to 3.5% in October, up from 2.8% in September.
cases.reasoning: CPI inflation 'rose to 3.5%' — inflation is the semantic object being measured. 'Annual CPI inflation' is the full subject phrase; inflation (or CPI) is the subject.

cases.text: The FCA imposed a financial penalty of £1.2 million on firm X for market abuse violations.
cases.reasoning: Penalty was 'imposed' with a measurement of £1.2 million. Penalty is the semantic object of the imposition event.

cases.text: Daily foreign exchange turnover averaged $4.6 trillion in April 2026, a 9% increase from October 2025.
cases.reasoning: FX turnover 'averaged $4.6 trillion' — FX is the measured object. The turnover is FX turnover, so FX is the semantic subject.

cases.text: Quarterly GDP advanced at a 2.7% annual rate, beating market expectations of 2.4%.
cases.reasoning: GDP 'advanced at 2.7%' — clear event verb + measurement. GDP is the subject.

cases.text: The ECB raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 4.50%, effective next Wednesday.
cases.reasoning: ECB 'raised its policy rate' — policy rate is the semantic object of the raising event. Basis points is a valid measurement.

cases.text: Headline CPI reached 4.2% year-over-year, the highest level since 2023.
cases.reasoning: CPI 'reached 4.2%' — CPI is the subject of the measurement event.

cases.text: The SEC announced a $5 million settlement with the firm over accounting irregularities.
cases.reasoning: Settlement of $5 million was 'announced' — settlement is the semantic object.

cases.text: Unemployment declined to 3.4% in November, the lowest reading since 1969.
cases.reasoning: Unemployment 'declined to 3.4%' — unemployment is the subject of the decline event.

cases.text: Inflation expectations eased to 2.1% for the medium term, closer to the central bank's target.
cases.reasoning: The subject is 'inflation expectations', not inflation itself. Inflation is a noun modifier of 'expectations'. Per V48X-style reasoning: expectations is the actual subject; inflation is the topic modifier.

cases.text: The PRA levied a financial penalty of £2.8 million on the bank for operational failures.
cases.reasoning: Penalty was 'levied' — clear event verb + measurement. Penalty is the subject.

cases.text: Foreign exchange turnover stabilized at $4.3 trillion in October, unchanged from April.
cases.reasoning: FX turnover 'stabilized at $4.3 trillion' — FX is the measured object. 'FX turnover' is the subject phrase; FX is the semantic subject.

cases.text: Real gross domestic product for the territory expanded 5.6% in 2025, exceeding forecasts.
cases.reasoning: GDP 'expanded 5.6%' — clear verb + measurement. GDP is the subject.

cases.text: The committee cut its policy rate by 50 basis points to 3.75%, citing improved inflation dynamics.
cases.reasoning: Policy rate was 'cut by 50 basis points' — policy rate is the subject of the cut event.

cases.text: Annual inflation slowed to 1.9% in the latest reading, finally reaching the 2% target zone.
cases.reasoning: Inflation 'slowed to 1.9%' — inflation is the subject.

cases.text: Bureau of Economic Analysis reported GDP rose 2.4% in Q3, driven by inventory investment.
cases.reasoning: GDP 'rose 2.4%' — GDP is the subject of the rise event.

cases.text: The regulator fined the firm $850,000 for late filing of regulatory reports.
cases.reasoning: Regulator 'fined the firm $850,000' — the fine/penalty is the subject of the action.

cases.text: FX volumes climbed 12% in the latest central bank survey, reaching a multi-year high.
cases.reasoning: FX volumes 'climbed 12%' — FX is the subject of the climb event. 'FX volumes' is the subject phrase.

cases.text: Policy Rate was maintained at 3.5% by unanimous committee vote, with no dissent.
cases.reasoning: Policy rate 'was maintained at 3.5%' — policy rate is the subject of the maintenance event.

cases.text: Consumer Price Index for the metropolitan area advanced 3.8% over the year, according to the latest data.
cases.reasoning: CPI 'advanced 3.8%' — CPI is the subject of the advance event.

cases.text: The central bank reduced its policy rate by 25 basis points to 2.0%, the first cut in 14 months.
cases.reasoning: Policy rate was 'reduced by 25 basis points' — policy rate is the subject of the reduction.

cases.text: Unemployment improved to 4.1% in December from 4.4% in November, indicating labor market cooling.
cases.reasoning: Unemployment 'improved to 4.1%' — unemployment is the subject of the improvement event.

cases.text: Penalty of $2.3 million finalized with the firm for compliance breach under regulatory framework.
cases.reasoning: Penalty 'finalized at $2.3 million' — penalty is the subject of the finalization event.

cases.text: Foreign exchange activity peaked at $5.8 trillion in October, the highest on record.
cases.reasoning: FX activity 'peaked at $5.8 trillion' — FX is the subject. 'FX activity' is the subject phrase.

cases.text: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 2.1% in Q2, the BEA reported.
cases.reasoning: GDP 'increased at 2.1%' — GDP is the subject of the increase event.

cases.text: Housing Starts Report. CPI is mentioned as backdrop in the economic overview.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Housing Starts' — clearly a different topic. CPI is mentioned only as backdrop. CPI is NOT the subject.

cases.text: Construction Spending. Policy Rate referenced as funding context.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Construction Spending' — different topic. Policy Rate is only referenced as context.

cases.text: Tourism Statistics. GDP noted in the broader economic comparison.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Tourism Statistics' — different topic. GDP is only noted in comparison.

cases.text: Patent Applications. Inflation cited as industry pricing factor.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Patent Applications' — different topic. Inflation is only cited as a factor.

cases.text: Aviation Statistics. FX turnover referenced in revenue context.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Aviation Statistics' — different topic. FX is only referenced in revenue context.

cases.text: Energy Production Report. CPI noted as commodity pricing reference.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Energy Production' — different topic. CPI is only a reference.

cases.text: Healthcare Statistics. Policy Rate referenced in insurance analysis.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Healthcare Statistics' — different topic. Policy Rate is referenced in analysis.

cases.text: Mining Sector Output. Unemployment cited as labor market factor.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Mining Sector Output' — different topic. Unemployment is cited as a factor.

cases.text: Education Spending Report. Inflation noted as budget context.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Education Spending' — different topic. Inflation is noted in budget context.

cases.text: Crime Statistics. Unemployment cited as social factor.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Crime Statistics' — different topic. Unemployment is cited as a social factor.

cases.text: FX turnover data is published semi-annually by the central bank.
cases.reasoning: 'FX turnover data is published' — the subject is 'data' (administrative), not FX. FX is a noun modifier of 'data' and 'turnover'. The event is administrative (publication schedule), not a measurement of FX.

cases.text: Penalty guidelines were issued for industry consultation.
cases.reasoning: Penalty is a noun modifier of 'guidelines'. The subject is 'guidelines', not penalty. Penalty is not the subject of an action here.

cases.text: Unemployment registrations increased 1.8% in Q3.
cases.reasoning: Unemployment is a noun modifier of 'registrations'. The subject is 'registrations' — they increased 1.8%, not unemployment itself.

cases.text: Policy Rate corridor was maintained as before, with no operational changes.
cases.reasoning: Policy Rate is a noun modifier of 'corridor'. The subject is 'corridor' (a structural feature of the rate framework), not the rate itself.

cases.text: GDP deflator was revised in the new methodology update.
cases.reasoning: GDP is a noun modifier of 'deflator'. The subject is 'deflator' (a measurement adjustment), not GDP itself.

cases.text: CPI basket was reviewed for representativeness in the upcoming rebase.
cases.reasoning: CPI is a noun modifier of 'basket'. The subject is 'basket' (the index composition), not CPI itself.

cases.text: Foreign exchange settlement systems were upgraded to modern standards.
cases.reasoning: FX is a noun modifier of 'settlement systems'. The subject is 'systems' (which were upgraded), not FX.

cases.text: Penalty framework was the subject of committee review last quarter.
cases.reasoning: Penalty is a noun modifier of 'framework'. The subject is 'framework' (reviewed by committee), not penalty itself.

cases.text: FX reserve buffers were described as adequate by the central bank governor.
cases.reasoning: FX is a noun modifier of 'reserve buffers'. The subject is 'buffers' (described as adequate), not FX itself.

cases.text: Trade Balance Report. GDP referenced in current-account analysis.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Trade Balance' — different topic. GDP is only referenced.

cases.text: Wage Growth Report. Inflation cited as comparison benchmark.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Wage Growth' — different topic. Inflation is only a comparison.

cases.text: Pension Statistics. Policy Rate noted in annuity calculation context.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Pension Statistics' — different topic. Policy Rate is only in annuity context.

cases.text: Retail Sales Report. Unemployment cited as consumer spending factor.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Retail Sales' — different topic. Unemployment is cited as a factor.

cases.text: Immigration Data. GDP mentioned in economic growth comparison.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Immigration Data' — different topic. GDP is mentioned in comparison.

cases.text: Manufacturing Output Report. Policy Rate noted in capital investment context.
cases.reasoning: Heading names 'Manufacturing Output' — different topic. Policy Rate is only noted in investment context.

cases.text: The bank noted that inflation pressures remain present, though moderating.
cases.reasoning: 'inflation pressures' — inflation is a noun modifier of 'pressures'. The subject is 'pressures'. But 'moderating' could apply to inflation indirectly. Genuinely ambiguous.

cases.text: GDP methodology was updated to reflect the new base year, with revisions to historical series.
cases.reasoning: GDP is a noun modifier of 'methodology'. The subject is 'methodology' (which was updated), not GDP itself.

cases.text: Policy Rate path will depend on incoming data, the committee noted.
cases.reasoning: Policy Rate is a noun modifier of 'path'. The subject is 'path' (will depend), not the rate itself.

cases.text: Unemployment figures were referenced in the staff briefing materials.
cases.reasoning: 'Unemployment figures were referenced' — the subject is 'figures', not unemployment itself. But the event is vague (referenced = no real action). Genuinely ambiguous.

cases.text: CPI print is scheduled for release next Tuesday per agency calendar.
cases.reasoning: CPI is a noun modifier of 'print'. The subject is 'print' (scheduled for release), not CPI itself.

cases.text: FX activity was described as orderly during the reporting period.
cases.reasoning: 'FX activity was described as orderly' — the subject is 'activity' (described), not FX directly. But 'orderly' could be a state-of-FX description. Ambiguous.

cases.text: Penalty provisions exist under the relevant enforcement framework.
cases.reasoning: Penalty is a noun modifier of 'provisions'. The subject is 'provisions' (which exist), not penalty itself.

cases.text: GDP estimates are subject to annual revision by the statistical office.
cases.reasoning: GDP is a noun modifier of 'estimates'. The subject is 'estimates' (which are subject to revision), not GDP itself.

cases.text: Inflation trajectory remains clouded by external factors and energy prices.
cases.reasoning: Inflation is a noun modifier of 'trajectory'. The subject is 'trajectory' (which remains clouded), not inflation itself.

cases.text: Policy Rate forward guidance was reiterated in the official statement.
cases.reasoning: Policy Rate is a noun modifier of 'forward guidance'. The subject is 'guidance' (reiterated), not the rate itself.

cases.text: The report identified unemployment as a continuing area of concern.
cases.reasoning: The report identified unemployment as a concern — unemployment is the object of identification. But this is a meta-statement, not a measurement event. Ambiguous.

cases.text: CPI measures came in beneath the central bank's 2% target band.
cases.reasoning: 'CPI measures came in beneath' — 'measures' is the subject, but it's specifically CPI measures. Could go either way. Ambiguous.

cases.text: Foreign exchange flows were characterized as stable and orderly.
cases.reasoning: 'FX flows were characterized as stable' — 'flows' is the subject, but it's specifically FX flows. Stable is a state-of-FX description. Ambiguous.

cases.text: Settlement discussions remain ongoing with the affected firm.
cases.reasoning: 'Settlement discussions' — settlement is a noun modifier of 'discussions'. The discussions are ongoing, but settlement itself is not yet finalized. Ambiguous.

cases.text: GDP dynamics featured prominently in the annual review.
cases.reasoning: GDP is a noun modifier of 'dynamics'. The subject is 'dynamics' (which featured), not GDP itself.

cases.text: Inflation developments were under continued close monitoring.
cases.reasoning: 'Inflation developments' — inflation is a noun modifier of 'developments'. 'Under monitoring' is administrative. Ambiguous.

cases.text: Policy Rate decisions will reflect incoming data shifts going forward.
cases.reasoning: Policy Rate is a noun modifier of 'decisions'. The subject is 'decisions' (will reflect), not the rate itself.

cases.text: Unemployment assistance was expanded under the new fiscal package.
cases.reasoning: Unemployment is a noun modifier of 'assistance'. The subject is 'assistance' (expanded), not unemployment itself.

cases.text: CPI weighting was refreshed for the new index series.
cases.reasoning: CPI is a noun modifier of 'weighting'. The subject is 'weighting' (refreshed), not CPI itself.

cases.text: FX reserve buffers were described as adequate by the central bank.
cases.reasoning: FX is a noun modifier of 'reserve buffers'. The subject is 'buffers' (described as adequate), not FX itself.

cases.text: The committee discussed GDP growth prospects at length during the meeting.
cases.reasoning: 'GDP growth prospects' — GDP is a noun modifier of 'prospects'. 'Discussed' is a meta-verb, not a measurement. Ambiguous.

cases.text: Inflation readings are projected to moderate in coming quarters per staff forecasts.
cases.reasoning: 'Inflation readings' — inflation is a noun modifier of 'readings'. 'Projected to moderate' is a forecast, not a current measurement. Ambiguous.

cases.text: Policy Rate stance will depend on incoming economic data, the bank said.
cases.reasoning: Policy Rate is a noun modifier of 'stance'. The subject is 'stance' (will depend), not the rate itself.

cases.text: The bank's statement cited unemployment as a labor market indicator to watch.
cases.reasoning: Unemployment is cited as an indicator to watch — not a measurement event. The bank is referencing unemployment, but no action/verb applies. Ambiguous.

cases.text: FX turnover statistics are compiled on a semi-annual basis per the survey schedule.
cases.reasoning: FX is a noun modifier of 'turnover statistics'. The subject is 'statistics' (compiled), not FX itself. Administrative event.

label_distribution.comment: Some 'positive' category cases are labeled CONTEXT by the human adjudicator (e.g., case 10 'Inflation expectations' — Inflation is a noun modifier of 'expectations'). This is intentional: the case category reflects expected engine output, but the human label is independent.
